title: Replace DOT discretionary grants with formula funding to states
proposal: DOT's discretionary grant programs should be abolished, with federal transportation money sent to states by formula so each state can choose its own priorities. At a minimum, grants should be consolidated.
quote: funding should be focused on formulaic distributions to the states, which know best their transportation needs and are incentivized to think of the

title: Revive DOT's "rule on rules" for regulations and guidance
proposal: DOT should bring back the 2019 Trump-era rule that set procedures for removing outdated regulations and made clear that guidance documents are not binding.
quote: “rule on rules” approach to regulations, implemented in late 2019 as RIN 2105-AE84

title: Require investment-grade ratings for Build America Bureau loans
proposal: The Build America Bureau should keep requiring borrowers to be rated investment grade and keep project sponsors liable for full repayment.
quote: maintaining the requirement that all project borrowers be rated at least investment grade by the major ratings agencies

title: Require economic value and equity stakes for federal infrastructure loans
proposal: Project sponsors seeking Build America Bureau loans should have to show positive economic value to taxpayers and put up a minimum equity commitment.
quote: Project sponsors should be required to show that projects have positive economic value to taxpayers, and sponsors should guarantee that all federal financing will be repaid

title: Test federal infrastructure loans against rising interest rates
proposal: All Build America Bureau projects should show they can repay under different interest rates, with loans structured to manage interest rate risk.
quote: All projects should also be required to show repayment ability in various interest rate environments,

title: Study whether federal infrastructure loans crowd out private lenders
proposal: A regular cost-benefit analysis should be done on whether federal infrastructure loans replace private financing.
quote: A cost-benefit analysis of the federal government’s potential replacement and disintermediation of the private financing sector regarding infrastructure loans,

title: Update vehicle safety rules for self-driving cars
proposal: NHTSA should remove regulatory barriers by updating vehicle standards and publishing performance-based rules for automated vehicles.
quote: NHTSA should work to remove regulatory barriers by focusing on updating vehicle standards as well as publishing performance-based rules for the operations of automated vehicles (AVs).

title: Allow driverless commercial trucks under federal rules
proposal: FMCSA should clarify its regulations, in line with DOT's AV 3.0 guidance, so drivers can be safely removed from commercial motor vehicles.
quote: FMCSA should work to clarify the regulations to align with DOT’s AV 3.0 guidance, which would allow the drivers to be safely removed

title: Reverse mandatory crash-data order for automated vehicles
proposal: DOT should reverse its Standing General Order requiring automated vehicle data collection and publication, returning to voluntary data sharing.
quote: through a Standing General Order related to automated vehicles. This needs to be reversed.

title: Push for more radio spectrum for transportation safety
proposal: DOT should represent the transportation community and argue to the public and Congress for spectrum needed for traffic safety technology.
quote: DOT needs to represent the transportation community and make the case for needed spectrum to the public and Congress.

title: Lower fuel economy (CAFE) standards to model year 2020 levels
proposal: The administration should consider returning fuel economy standards to the levels Congress set for model year 2020 cars, aimed at a 35 mpg fleet average, and keep them there for the near term.
quote: The Administration should consider returning to the minimum average fuel economy levels specified by Congress for model year 2020 vehicles:

title: Give DOT priority over EPA on fuel economy
proposal: Any EPA limits on vehicle carbon dioxide emissions should work with DOT's fuel economy standards and not override them.
quote: Any EPA limits on carbon dioxide emissions, even if authorized under the Clean Air Act, must support and work in harmony with DOT standards and must not override them

title: Revoke California's Clean Air Act vehicle waiver
proposal: The federal government should revoke California's waiver and act to invalidate California fuel economy requirements, including its planned ban on sales of gas-powered cars.
quote: Revoke the special waiver granted to California by the Biden Administration. California has no valid basis under the Clean Air Act

title: Refocus the Federal Highway Administration on highways
proposal: The next administration should refocus FHWA on maintaining and improving the highway system rather than other priorities.
quote: Seek to refocus the FHWA on maintaining and improving the highway system.

title: Reduce federal role in local infrastructure decisions
proposal: The administration should remove or reform rules that hamper state governments and reduce federal involvement in local infrastructure decisions.
quote: Reduce the amount of federal involvement in local infrastructure decisions.

title: Restore Trump-era process for airline consumer protection rules
proposal: DOT should restore the Trump-era procedures for issuing "unfair and deceptive practices" rules for airlines, which the Biden administration reversed.
quote: The Trump Administration reformed the process for issuing such “unfair and deceptive practices” rules,9 but the Biden Administration promptly reversed those reforms.
agency: DOT / Office of Aviation Consumer Protection

title: Support joint ventures by smaller airlines
proposal: The administration should publicly support joint ventures by smaller airlines, such as JetBlue and Spirit, so they can compete with larger carriers.
quote: Publicly indicate that a new Administration would support joint-venture efforts by smaller carriers (for example, Jet Blue and Spirit)

title: Loosen foreign ownership limits on U.S. airlines
proposal: The administration should review foreign ownership limits on airlines and, if needed, work with Congress to allow investment from like-minded countries while U.S. investors keep plurality ownership.
quote: Review foreign ownership and control limitations and, if necessary, work with Congress to change existing statutes.

title: Decide new airline applications within 12 months
proposal: A New Entry Initiative should commit the government to approve or reject new airline applications within 12 months.
quote: Establish a New Entry Initiative that commits the federal government to approving or rejecting the applications of new air carriers within 12 months.

title: Rewrite airport slot allocation rules
proposal: DOT should start a rulemaking to allocate takeoff and landing slots at crowded airports based mainly on safety, capacity, and competition.
quote: Initiate a rulemaking to allocate slot-pairs more consistently to airlines at capacity-controlled airports on the primary basis of safety, maximizing capacity, and competition.

title: Reduce flight-hour requirements for copilots
proposal: The chapter suggests copilots could be required to have fewer than 1,500 flight hours or be allowed to count certified simulator training.
quote: This trend could be reversed if copilots were required to have fewer flight hours or could count certified simulator training.

title: End the Essential Air Service subsidy program
proposal: The chapter says ending the Essential Air Service program, which subsidizes flights to about 200 small airports, would free pilots for larger markets.
quote: Finally ending the program would free hundreds of pilots to serve larger markets with more passengers.

title: Limit foreign airlines that fly over Russia to the U.S.
proposal: While U.S. airlines cannot fly over Russia, the U.S. should not let foreign airlines serving East and South Asia gain an advantage by continuing to fly to the U.S.
quote: so long as U.S. carriers are not able to fly over Russian airspace, the U.S. should not allow foreign carriers serving markets in East Asia and South Asia

title: Pause new aviation talks with China
proposal: The U.S. should not offer new aviation negotiations until China carries out the agreements it has already signed.
quote: not offer additional negotiations until the Chinese implement the agreements they have already signed.

title: Create an interagency clearinghouse on drones and air mobility
proposal: The administration should set up an interagency clearinghouse for consistent policy on spectrum, drones, and advanced air mobility.
quote: the new Administration should establish an interagency clearinghouse to drive consistent policies across the government on spectrum, drones, and advanced air mobility.

title: Get the FAA out of research and development
proposal: The FAA should stop doing research and development and instead test, evaluate, and certify private-sector innovation faster.
quote: It should get out of the R&D business and focus on testing, evaluating, and certifying private-sector innovation much more quickly than it does today.

title: Set professional requirements for top FAA leaders
proposal: The FAA should consider promoting top executives from within and setting strict professional requirements for its top appointees.
quote: consider promoting the FAA’s top executive team from within and requiring strict professional requirements for its top appointees.

title: Separate the FAA from DOT or air traffic control from the FAA
proposal: The FAA should be separated from DOT or, at a minimum, its Air Traffic Organization should be separated from the FAA.
quote: Separate the FAA from DOT or, at a minimum, separate the ATO from the FAA.

title: Take FAA funding off annual appropriations
proposal: The FAA's funding system should be completely restructured so aviation does not depend on yearly appropriations.
quote: Completely restructure the FAA’s funding system so that the nation’s aviation system is not held prisoner to annual appropriations

title: Make the FAA operate more like a business
proposal: The FAA should operate more like a business, using its special authority over personnel and purchasing.
quote: Require the FAA to operate more like a business. The FAA has not made good use of the unique authority it has been given

title: Move air traffic control headquarters outside Washington, D.C.
proposal: The Air Traffic Organization should be separated from the FAA and given headquarters outside the District of Columbia. This requires legislation.
quote: Separate the ATO from the FAA and relocate it to separate headquarters outside the District of Columbia.

title: Fund air traffic control with user fees instead of taxes
proposal: Aviation user taxes should be replaced with fees for air traffic services paid directly to the Air Traffic Organization.
quote: Shift from aviation user taxes to fees for air traffic services paid directly to the ATO.

title: Let air traffic control issue revenue bonds
proposal: Congress should allow the Air Traffic Organization to issue long-term revenue bonds for major projects.
quote: Allow the ATO to issue long-term revenue bonds for major projects.

title: Charge fees to new airspace users and phase out analog towers
proposal: Congress could require user fees for new airspace users like air taxis and space launches and set a deadline after which no new non-digital control towers are funded.
quote: implementing user fees for unconventional airspace users (for example, advanced air mobility, space launch, and recovery) and giving the ATO a deadline

title: Redefine public transit to include private services
proposal: Congress should define public transit as transit provided for the public, not only by a government, so services like rideshare could count.
quote: A better definition for public transit (which also would require congressional legislation) would be transit provided for the public rather than transit provided by a public municipality.

title: Require cost-benefit tests for transit expansion grants
proposal: The chapter notes past calls to eliminate the Capital Investment Grants program and says, at a minimum, each project should meet sound economic standards and a strict cost-benefit test.
quote: At a minimum, a new conservative Administration should ensure that each CIG project meets sound economic standards and a rigorous cost-benefit analysis.

title: Reinterpret transit labor protections to allow benefit changes
proposal: Section 10(c) of the 1964 transit law should be returned to its original intent so transit agencies can adjust fringe benefits without fear of a federal lawsuit.
quote: Returning to the original intent would allow transit agencies to adjust fringe

title: End federal transit subsidies from the Highway Trust Fund
proposal: The federal government should stop using the Highway Trust Fund to support mass transit and remove federal transit subsidies, leaving transit decisions to states and localities.
quote: the best course of action would be to remove federal subsidies for transit spending, allowing states and localities to decide whether mass transit is a good investment for them.

title: Drop proposed two-person train crew rule
proposal: The chapter criticizes FRA's proposed rule requiring at least two crew members on trains as not based on safety, among actions FRA should review.
quote: FRA’s Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) on crew size is not based on safety considerations;

title: Modernize railroad track inspection rules
proposal: FRA should update 50-year-old track inspection requirements to allow technology-based inspection.
quote: it is refusing to amend 50-year-old track inspection requirements, leaving customers with higher costs.

title: Finish rule allowing electronic brake inspection records
proposal: FRA should finish a rule letting railroads track brake inspections electronically and extend inspection intervals.
quote: FRA is refusing to take final action on a rulemaking proceeding that would modernize brake inspection requirements

title: Do not require certification for rail dispatchers and signal staff
proposal: The chapter criticizes planned FRA certification requirements for dispatchers and signal workers, saying no safety benefit was identified.
quote: FRA will be proposing certification requirements for dispatchers and signal employees despite the failure of the Railroad Safety Advisory Committee

title: Do not require breathing apparatus for train crews
proposal: The chapter criticizes planned FRA emergency breathing equipment rules for train crews as costing far more than their benefits.
quote: FRA is planning to propose emergency escape breathing apparatus requirements for train crews even though FRA staff long ago concluded

title: Award rail research money on merit
proposal: FRA should decide where to spend research money only on how well it improves railroad safety and efficiency.
quote: FRA should make its decisions on where to spend its research dollars solely on the merits of improving the safety and efficiency of the railroad industry.

title: Move the Maritime Administration out of DOT
proposal: The Maritime Administration and the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy should move from DOT to the Department of Homeland Security, or to Defense if the Coast Guard moves there.
quote: MARAD, including its subordinate Service Academy (the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy) should be transferred to the Department of Defense

title: Consider repealing or reforming the Jones Act
proposal: Serious consideration should be given to repealing or greatly reforming the Jones Act shipping law, which would require legislation.
quote: Serious consideration should be given to repealing or substantially reforming the Jones Act
